headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold a narrow two-sided overnight band as the Bank of Japan statement window opens on quarterly expiration day
body:
NQ is trading at 29,677.75, down about 65 points or 0.22%, inside a 29,648.50-29,728.50 overnight band as of 02:16 UTC. The band spans only 80 points, or 0.27%, and the structure is two-sided: the marginal new low at 29,648.50 was rejected and bought back roughly 29 points, so retracement is functioning and price is not holding a session extreme. That is the most important current observation, because a persistent no-retracement path is what the Tail score measures, and it is absent.

The backdrop is unusually aligned on the bullish side, but as latest-session rather than live evidence. The cash Nasdaq-100 closed Thursday at 29,446.98, up 1.73%, near the top of its 29,305.90-29,494.95 range, fully retracing the slump that followed Wednesday's Federal Reserve decision to raise the target range by 25bp to 3.75-4.00%, its first hike since 2023. All eight tracked megacaps closed higher with tight dispersion, and all seven tracked semiconductors closed higher by an average of 5.0%. The VIX fell 12.8% to 15.44, closing at the low of its range. Under the shared-context rules this alignment is confirmation evidence only; it cannot establish live NQ structure on its own.

Cross-asset conditions are cooperative rather than confirming a one-way trend. WTI is $101.34, down 0.56%, and Brent $104.15, down 0.64%, a third consecutive decline as US-Iran supply concerns ease and diplomacy resumes; that reduces the inflation-shock channel into rate-sensitive Nasdaq leadership even though the absolute level remains high. The latest H.15 constant-maturity readings are 4.74% at two years and 5.01% at ten years as of 16 September; a live intraday yield refresh was not obtainable this run, and the shared Finviz futures section was unavailable.

Two structural items define the day ahead. The Bank of Japan statement is expected near 03:00 UTC with Governor Ueda's press conference at 06:30 UTC; a 25bp hike to 1.25% is largely priced, so the conditional risk lies in pace guidance transmitting through the yen, and the statement-then-press-conference shape gives it a credible delayed second leg. Today is also a quarterly expiration, which concentrates roll and closing-imbalance flow into the US session and the 20:00 UTC settlement.

On this evidence Tail is 17% and Stress 40%. Elevated event density and an orderly price path coexist here by design: the calendar is dense, but nothing has printed yet and the observed structure is mean-reverting. Tail remains well below the 25% block threshold. Mapped policy state: EA_ON.

lookbackSummary: All 24 hours to 01:00 UTC are covered by published Claude assessments. Tail opened at 19% during Thursday's Asian session, peaked at 26% in the 13:00 UTC hour around the US cash open - the only hour in the window that mapped to an orange BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES state - and then eased steadily to 17-18% overnight. Stress fell almost continuously from 69% to 41% as the repricing that followed Wednesday's 25bp Federal Reserve hike resolved in an orderly way and implied volatility decayed, with the VIX closing at 15.44, down 12.8%. The dominant mode ran mixed through the early Asian hours, turned trend-up from 07:00 UTC as the cash session rallied 1.73%, and reverted to normal from 22:00 UTC once futures reopened into a narrow two-sided band. Confidence held in a tight 85-88% range throughout, reflecting continuous coverage rather than any single strong signal.
outlookSummary: The projected path holds 17% in the current hour, then steps into the watch band for the Bank of Japan sequence: 22% as the statement is expected near 03:00 UTC, easing through the 05:00 UTC lull, and returning to a 23% Asian-session peak at 07:00 UTC for the press-conference Q&A and the delayed cross-asset reaction. It falls back to 17-18% across the European morning before the day's conditional peak of 24% in the 14:00 UTC hour, the first full hour of quarterly-expiration cash trade following a session that closed with 8 of 8 megacaps and 7 of 7 semiconductors higher. Two further watch steps follow at 19:00 and 20:00 UTC for the closing imbalance and quarterly settlement. From 21:00 UTC the CME weekend halt removes any tradeable price path, so projected Tail falls to 8-10% across the final five slots and Stress settles into the low band. Every level beyond the current hour is conditional: no post-event or post-open structure is observed yet.
